correctness.rationale: For a proper coloring of Cr_n=K_{n,n}-M_n, any shared color occupies precisely one deleted matching pair. If s such pairs are colored distinctly, remaining colors are shore-exclusive. Each open neighborhood equals an opposite shore minus its matched vertex: with s>=2 every puncture retains a singleton, with s=1 at least one extra exclusive singleton is needed, and with s=0 the shore has either at least two singleton fibers or all classes doubletons. The labeled-surjection counts S_{m,r}, B_{m,r}, E_{m,r}=r m B_{m-1,r-1}, H_{m,r}=m!/2^r when m=2r have exactly those meanings. Summing binomial choices and falling-factorial assignments proves the entire P_n(q) for all n>=3, q>=0; n=4,q=4 splits s=0,2,4 into 216+144+24=384 and for n>=5,q=4 only s=2 survives, yielding 24*binom(n,2). Direct independent brute-force counted (n,q)=(3,3):6, (3,4):96, (4,4):384, (5,4):240, recording their shared-color strata; all agree with the source, but finite checks are not the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The chromatic-number bound and complete-multipartite enumeration do not enumerate Cr_n=K_{n,n} minus a matching; its missing-pair adjacency is not a complete multipartite graph. The published chi proof gives only a feasible four-color pattern and minimum color count.
